title: refactor: replace QString() with QStringLiteral() for better performance
description: Qt provides a macro `QStringLiteral()`, which makes constructing `QString` objects from string literals more efficient.

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/17795/diffs?diff_id=1162322906&start_sha=6765edab8c04f0a41cc54baa215855a33ebdba8e)
I am seeing in Protocol Port Preferences mojibake with â, which probably not coincidentally is Latin-1 0xE2, with UTF-8 for Horizontal Ellipsis being 0xE2 0x80 0xA6.
Could you give me a screenshot of the mojibake?

Will do, it's on a RHEL9 box with Qt 6.6.2 from EPEL.

It works if the entries in `wsutil/utf8_entities.h` is changed from hex character literals to a literal UTF-8 horizontal ellipsis. It looks like QStringLiteral macro does some direct casts to `char16_t *` in at least some cases (might depend on the compiler), which works with literals but not hex characters.

Here it is in Fedora. You can see that the hex characters for the horizontal ellipsis are interpreted as Latin-1 (or possibly UTF-16) instead of UTF-8:  
![Screenshot_from_2024-10-28_18-06-14](/uploads/7af0a06e9f5f334691f63c8d90c2e536/Screenshot_from_2024-10-28_18-06-14.png)

https://github.com/qt/qtbase/blob/dev/src/corelib/text/qstringliteral.h

QStringLiteral calls `QT_UNICODE_LITERAL(str)`, which is defined as `u"" str`, which is fine for strings without prefixes that use literal UTF-8 characters (if the compiler expects the source to be UTF-8; the encoding of the source file does not have to match the interpretation of the string) as conversion of the code point occurs, but causes literal hex bytes to be interpreted as UTF-16 (because if an ordinary string literal is adjacent to a UTF-16 (`u`) string literal, the latter is interpreted as UTF-16), which is wrong. If the entries in `utf8_entities.h` are prefixed with `u8`, then there is an error because the program is ill-formed with UTF-16 and UTF-8 string literals next to each other.
